reason: Compound rule; weighted the operative conduct clauses (two-verdict completeness in substance, no pre-judging, pushback with technical reasoning, detecting a test narrowed to fit the implementation) — each requires judging the MEANING of review findings and whether a test still asserts the planned scenario; a section-header scan of a review report could see two headings but not two verdicts.

cost: It is a lookup table mapping past failures to the gates that now catch them — a documentation index; enforcing it would mean enforcing each referenced gate, which each has its own rule.
importance: בינונית — high explanatory value (it justifies the gates and teaches the failure shapes) but carries no compliance condition of its own.

reason: Compound: 'no English leak' on a rendered DOM is near-mechanical, but the operative requirement — correct singular/plural on interpolated counts and correct domain term, verified on a rendered screen — requires linguistic and domain judgment of the rendered text's meaning; weighted that clause.

cost: A retrospective declaration of personal commitments; each of its six items restates a rule enforced elsewhere (evidence pasting, 390px screenshots, escalation, flaky=bug, diff verification), so enforcing it separately duplicates those gates without adding a compliance condition of its own.
importance: בינונית — valuable as the lessons-anchor that motivated the real gates, but as text it is a record of intent, not a checkable requirement.

cost: A historical failure record (what happened, root cause, which gate now covers it); there is nothing to comply with — the enforceable content lives in the Waiver Gate rule it points to.
importance: נמוכה כרשומה, גבוהה כהקשר — it is the origin story of the most important gate, but itself carries no condition.

reason: Deciding whether a plan 'waives, defers, or reinterprets' an approved spec requirement requires comparing the semantic content of plan text against spec text — a token scan for 'deferred'/'waived' misses reinterpretation and narrowing entirely (and the founding failure was a rewording, not a keyword); whether a change was 'raised in conversation' is intent/context, not a textual pattern.

Compound: the presence of a verbatim spec quote in the task report is mechanically checkable, but the operative requirement — that the quoted line genuinely covers THIS task ('if none → the task should not exist') and, for ⚠️R items, that the relevance verdict rests on real current-code evidence — requires judging the relationship between spec meaning and the work; weighted that clause.

Every clause (hardest-constraint identification, pre-mortem plausibility, MECE requirement-to-task mapping, reversibility classification, ambiguity of nouns/verbs in briefs, acceptability of low-confidence risks) is an evaluation of a plan's meaning and quality — no artifact pattern decides any of them.

artifact: the Agent-dispatch payload plus the brief FILE it names under .superpowers/sdd/ (template docs/process/templates/task-brief.md)
pattern: an implementation dispatch must reference a brief file whose required sections — quoted spec lines (a), plan code (b), DoD checklist (c), report contract incl. H9 table (d), primary-tool field (e) — are present and non-placeholder; a missing/TODO field = invalid brief (make-brief.mjs already refuses exactly this)
reason: Compound rule: the Main-vs-subagent division-of-labor table needs judgment, but the operative requirement the rule enforces in practice is the brief/report file contract, whose field-presence structure is mechanically decidable — weighted that clause.

Deciding that a diff introduces a 'new derived/computed value', that a named reader is in production code, and (per L8) that the reader actually fires on real data is semantic code analysis — reference-existence can be greppable but 'real consumer on the runtime path' is a meaning judgment (the rule exists precisely because dead readers look like readers).

Compound umbrella rule: the presence of 12 evidence sections in a report is checkable, but the operative requirement is that each box is satisfied WITH valid evidence — behavioural assertion, fixture minimality, safety invariance and 'evidence actually proves it' (L45) all require judging what the pasted output means; weighted the evidence-validity clause over the section-presence clause.

mechanism_target: git commit touching tests/** together with implementation files
observed_prior_facts: the recorded tool-use sequence since the last commit — a run of the new test observed exiting non-zero BEFORE the implementation edit, then a passing run after (test-run outcomes and edit ordering observed via posttooluse logs / the state store)
reason: Compound: the operative requirement is the SEQUENCE (test written first, observed failing, then made green) which is prior-event knowledge, not a static artifact pattern; the residual clause 'failing for the intended reason' is judgment — weighted the sequence clause.

cost: It documents the three invocation forms of the /status command — a feature description; the only mechanical check imaginable is 'the command file exists', which is not what the text requires of anyone.
importance: נמוכה — useful reference, no compliance condition.

mechanism_target: docs/ROADMAP-2026-07-30.md §5a Recovery Ledger rows vs first implementation commits of ⚠️R work
observed_prior_facts: whether the picked-up ⚠️R row already carries a recorded owner-approved verdict (בצע/בטל) before any implementation work lands, and that a cancelled row was marked R-cancelled rather than deleted
reason: Compound: the operative requirement is order — owner checkpoint and ledger update BEFORE implementation — which is prior-event knowledge readable from the ledger file (the state store); whether the verdict's supporting evidence is sound is a residual judgment clause — weighted the sequencing clause.

'Only what the scenario needs' is a judgment about the relationship between fixture content and scenario intent — no pattern distinguishes a minimal fixture from one smuggling in the accessory the broken gate needed; whether 'the negative case' was tested requires knowing what the negative case IS.

Deciding whether an assertion targets an 'observable effect a real consumer reads' versus a computed field nothing consumes requires understanding what the asserted value means in the program — the same assert() call is compliant or void depending on semantics invisible to any textual pattern.

pattern: presence of an explicit, non-empty model (and effort) field in every subagent dispatch — absence = the forbidden silent inheritance
reason: Compound: the bolded operative demand is 'המודל נבחר מפורשות, לעולם לא בירושה שקטה', which field-presence decides mechanically; the residual clauses (model matches task type per the table; no retroactive escalation after success) need task-nature judgment and dispatch history — weighted the explicitness clause.

Deciding compliance means judging whether a given task WAS 'single-task with one clear requirement', an 'obvious single-cause bug', or 'following an established pattern' — i.e. evaluating the nature and difficulty of the work before knowing whether ceremony was waste; no artifact pattern or prior-event record decides it.

artifact: the owner-facing gate-prompt tool payload (the question/options structure observed in the tool's hook payload)
pattern: options array length ≤ 4, header string ≤ 12 characters, multi-select flag absent/false for gates, and an 'Other'/freeform option handled per the named shapes
reason: The operative constraints are numeric/structural properties of the prompt payload itself — decidable without reading intent; posttooluse chosen because the prompting tool has no dedicated pretooluse entry in the closed vocabulary (compound edge: 'handle the freeform answer' is behavioral, but the counts/lengths carry the rule).
